content: backdrop-filter over a LIVE animated WebGL canvas is the worst case: the backdrop changes every frame so the browser cannot cache the blurred texture — it must re-sample the canvas region, render to an offscreen buffer, run Gaussian convolution, and re-composite each frame. Cost scales with blur radius (blur(20px) is severalx blur(4px) in GPU bandwidth) and with number of stacked glass elements. Ancestors with overflow:hidden/clip-path/mask or will-change:opacity can break or disable backdrop-filter by isolating compositing layers. Mitigation: downsample background to 1/4 or 1/8 before blurring (~16x less work, imperceptible on moving backgrounds), keep blur radius modest, avoid nesting glass over glass.
